plain_english_policy: This bill prevents Alabama state agencies from creating rules to limit greenhouse gas emissions, regulate how fuel-efficient cars must be, or start a cap-and-trade system unless the Legislature explicitly passes new laws authorizing those specific actions first. It requires an impact study on costs and businesses before any such program can become legal.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The enactment of this bill would centralize authority over environmental regulations regarding motor vehicles in the hands of the elected legislature, effectively blocking executive branch agencies from acting unilaterally to reduce emissions or implement market-based trading schemes without prior legislative approval and a fiscal impact analysis.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced the bill to prohibit state agencies from regulating motor vehicle fuel economy or implementing cap and trade programs without express legislative authorization.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would prohibit a state agency from limiting or regulating greenhouse gas emissions or motor vehicle fuel economy, or from implementing a cap and trade program, without express legislative authorization."

"It is the intent of the Legislature that... a state or regional program to implement a cap and trade system or any other program to address greenhouse gas emissions or motor vehicle fuel economy... must receive express legislative authorization"
